claims.claim: SQM's July 2026 Form 6-K filed on SEC EDGAR reports that SQM and Wesfarmers jointly approved the final investment decision for the Mt Holland lithium expansion; the project covers the mine, concentrator and a new integrated ore-sorting facility and is intended to double spodumene concentrate production while lowering unit operating costs.
claims.risk: The source establishes committed expansion and intended scale/cost benefits, but not realized returns, commissioning success or future lithium clearing prices.
claims.falsifier: Material construction delay, cost overrun, weak utilization or failure to lower unit operating costs would invalidate the intended execution benefit.

factors: intended doubling of spodumene concentrate production
unknowns: The filing does not establish realized project returns, final delivered cost, commissioning outcome or future lithium pricing.
This assist does not assign Alpha numeric underwriting values or data-confidence scores.
recommendedNextState: council-alpha should reuse the SEC-filed project facts as source-addressed factor/risk evidence while retaining numeric underwriting authority

doctrine.observedWeakness: multi-year project execution remains unproven until delivered
doctrine.uncertainty: realized cost, schedule, utilization and lithium-cycle economics
doctrine.possibleImprovement: demonstrated on-budget/on-schedule delivery with lower unit costs and durable utilization
doctrine.evidenceNeeded: subsequent construction, commissioning, unit-cost, utilization and project-return disclosures
